title: Musician, Vocalist (GySgt to Pvt) NMOS (5524), DIR COMM
raw_text:
23.     MOS 5567, Musician, Vocalist (GySgt to Pvt) NMOS (5524), DIR COMM

    a. Summary. Vocalists perform in a Marine Corps Band for concerts,
ceremonies, small ensembles, as a soloist, and various other official
functions in support of the Marine Corps Bands’ mission. Vocalists perform
additional duties in support of band operations, such as unit supply, unit
administrative assistant, and music librarian. Additional increased
responsibilities relating to music performance are assigned based on grade/
experience, such as instrumental group leader or leader of a small ensemble.
Vocalists may be assigned to complete the Live Production Technician Course
and be assigned additional duties of sound engineer.

       b.   Prerequisites.   Must possess MOS 5524.



                                         3-323                       Enclosure (1)
 3134                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



       c.   Requirements

            (1) Must be a proficient vocalist.

        (2) Must be capable of performing basic percussion or other relevant
instrument with the ceremonial marching band.

    d. Duties. For a complete list of duties and tasks, refer to reference
(be), Music Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Musician and Singers 27-2042.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Member, "The President's Own," U.S. Marine Band, 5511.

            (2) Member, "The Commandant's Own," U.S. Marine Drum and Bugle Corps.




                                        3-324                        Enclosure (1)
 3135                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L
common_text: Marines in the Music OccFld provide music to support military ceremonies, official functions, community relations, personnel procurement programs, theater security cooperation, and troop "esprit de corps”. In combat, musical units continue musical functions and augment security on a temporary basis during periods of heightened combat intensity when use of the band in its primary role is impractical. Marines entering this OccFld will receive MOS 5500, Basic Musician. All OccFld 5500 MOSs are assigned and voided by authority of the CMC (MM). Marines enlisting under the Musician Enlistment Option Program (MEOP) U2 will be required to attend the Basic Music Course at the Naval School of Music (NSOM) after having completed recruit training and Marine Combat Training (MCT). Assignment to a Marine Corps Band follows successful completion of the Music Basic Course. Career Marine musicians will return to the NSOM for required advanced technical training or complete the Instrument Repair Course provided through a civilian school. The opportunity to participate in a formal apprenticeship program leading to receipt of department of labor certification of apprenticeship may be available in some MOSs within OccFld 55.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade.
